reasoning: NotificationService.deliveryFinished: after a failure it asks the OS for the permission status. Only .denied sets authorizationKnownDenied and leaves the crossing marked. .notDetermined, the first-crossing case from CQ-MAE-012, still re-arms. The flag changes only whether a failed crossing is re-armed. Every new crossing still calls center.add, and one successful delivery clears the flag (`guard let failure else { authorizationKnownDenied = false }`). So a user who grants permission later is not locked out: the next crossing is delivered and the cache clears. Caveat, not a vote reason: a crossing that failed while permission was denied stays marked after the user grants, so that one threshold is not re-sent until the window resets or a higher threshold is reached. That is the intended trade-off against retrying on every tick. Reversals: with the guard removed and the .denied branch disabled, 'a failure while authorization is denied does not re-arm' went RED (:119) and so did 'a known denial is cached' (statusQueries 2 == 1, :145). With the clear-on-success line removed, 'a delivery after a cached denial clears it' went RED (:163).
